title: While they're out partying…
summary: Show off one oddly specific, totally useless skill under the caption "While they're out partying…". AI helps you pick the skill and write the line.
why: Know Your Meme added the "While they're out partying" entry on October 21, 2026. It lists October posts in this format with millions of views within days, where creators show a useless skill they've mastered under that caption.
steps: Use the main prompt to brainstorm useless skills you already have, or could learn in an afternoon.
Pick the one that looks best on camera and practise it a few times.
Film it in one take, straight on, with good light. Deadpan works best.
Add the caption from the prompt as on-screen text and post it as a Reel or TikTok.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: I'm making a short video for the "While they're out partying…" trend, where you show off a skill that's oddly specific and completely useless. Here's a bit about me: [hobbies, job, things I'm weirdly good at]. Give me 10 skill ideas I could film at home in under a minute, nothing dangerous. For each one, write the on-screen caption in the style "While they're out partying, I [skill]". Keep each caption under 15 words and rank them by how funny they'd look on camera.

prompts.label: Variation: learn one this weekend
prompts.text: Suggest 8 harmless, oddly specific skills I could learn in one afternoon with things already in my kitchen or junk drawer, for a "While they're out partying…" video. For each one, give me 3 quick practice steps and the caption to put on screen.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run [your type of business]. Write 8 captions for a "While they're out partying…" video showing the oddly specific, behind-the-scenes skills my job needs, like [an example task]. Keep it playful and true to how we really work. Don't make up numbers, reviews or results.

tips: The more specific the skill, the funnier it lands. Folding a fitted sheet beats "cleaning".
Don't smile or explain. Let the caption do the joke.
Keep it safe: no stunts, knives, fire or anything you'd regret.
For a business, a satisfying close-up of a real task works really well.
